newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: Strong foreign and local buying, spurred by hopes of a cut soon in South Africa's interest rates lifted industrial shares to new highs in heavy turnover trade on Wednesday.
Dealers and fund managers said that South African equities were looking relatively cheap to overseas buyers, further sweetened by the likelihood of a rate reduction.
"In international terms we are looking cheap compared with other emerging markets," said Rhett Hammond, a portfolio manager at Investec Asset Management.
"An interest rate cut would just be an extra good reason to buy," he said.
Rate reduction hopes, which have been powering the market since early June, were reflected in strong gains in interest-sensitive financial shares.
Stanbic, the country's second biggest bank, added 300 cents to close at 219.00 rand after reporting within-expectation half year results on Tuesday and anticipated a robust second half.

Large offshore deals in diversified industrial company Barlow and fuels firm Sasol -- appealing also for its hedge against the weaker rand -- pushed the day's takings to a well-above-average 1.1 billion rand.
Dealers said the rand's slide to fresh 6 -1/2 month lows on Wednesday was shrugged off as a function of a rampant U.S. dollar.
The industrial index ended up 64.1 points at 9,247.1, hoisting the all share index 54.1 points higher to 7,546.8.
Gold and platinum shares weathered an overnight fall in precious metal prices helped by the weaker rand which raises the rand metal price mines' receive.
The gold index rose 2.5 points to 956.5 and the platinum index 20.1 to 5,552.4.
Another rand hedge to gain was container firm Mobile which added 10 percent to 190 cents in busy trade. Volumes on the Mobile stock were last at 4.3 million rand.
Snacks and confectionary firm Afribrand rushed up in busy trade after its strong debut on Tuesday after the firm issued a cautionary that it was in talks.
It ended 22 percent up at 276 cents.
Electronics firm Daewoo slid heavily, but ended off the day's worst levels, after a profit warning on Tuesday. It ended at 196 cents, off 34 cents.
Embattled clothing firm Sterling jumped 33 percent to 40 cents on news an investment company had bought a controlling stake in it and planned to cut its debt levels.
In the broader market advancing issues led declining issues by 205 to 164, while 36 shares surged to new highs and 14 dipped to new lows.
Equity index futures soared in hectic dealings propelled by gains on the stock market and a retracement from weaker levels on the bond market, dealers said.
"There has been lots of demand today, especially from overseas," a futures dealer said.
The South African industrial September contract was last at 8,790/95 from 8,659 settlement, the gold near month at 672/80 from 674 settlement and the all-share contract at 6,780/95 from 6,695.
-- Nicole Mordant, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003 -- E-mail: johannesburg.newsroom@reuters.com
